Who it's for

What people get wrong

Buying ravintsara by mistake, or the reverse. Ravensara aromatica and Ravintsara (Cinnamomum camphora) are different plants with similar names, routinely mislabelled across the industry. Check the botanical name.

Expecting it to be strong. It is one of the milder oils in this category, which is the point, but people who want eucalyptus should buy eucalyptus.

What it won't do

Not for babies or young children. And given how often ravensara and ravintsara are confused in the supply chain, ask us what we hold if it matters to you.

Questions about Ravensara

Is ravensara the same as ravintsara?

No, and it is one of the most persistent mix-ups in the industry. Ravensara aromatica is in the Lauraceae family from Madagascar; ravintsara is a Cinnamomum camphora chemotype. The names are close enough that mislabelling is common.

How does it compare to eucalyptus?

Milder and sweeter, with a faint aniseed note eucalyptus lacks. If eucalyptus feels too sharp, this is the gentler option.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. Not suitable for babies or young children. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.
